title: Computer Networks OSI 7-Layer Model, Sliding Window & Marked Price

sem_data.subject: BCA-5003 Computer Network
sem_data.topic: Unit I — OSI 7-Layer Reference Model vs TCP/IP Protocol Suite
detailed_notes: The Open Systems Interconnection (OSI) Reference Model was established by the International Organization for Standardization (ISO) in 1984 as a conceptual framework for computer-to-computer network communications. It divides network communication into seven distinct hierarchical layers, each providing services to the layer above and consuming services from the layer below.

Layer-by-Layer Architectural Responsibilities:
1. Physical Layer (Layer 1): Transmits raw, unstructured bitstreams over a physical transmission medium. Defines electrical, optical, and mechanical specifications (cables, voltages, pinouts, hubs, bit-rate).
2. Data Link Layer (Layer 2): Responsible for node-to-node (hop-by-hop) reliable data transfer across a physical link. Packages bits into Frames, manages physical addressing (MAC addresses), handles flow control, and performs error detection (CRC).
3. Network Layer (Layer 3): Responsible for host-to-host packet delivery across heterogeneous networks. Handles logical addressing (IPv4/IPv6), routing table maintenance, packet forwarding, and congestion control (Routers operate here).
4. Transport Layer (Layer 4): Delivers end-to-end (process-to-process) communication between applications. Handles port addressing, segmentation and reassembly, connection control (TCP 3-way handshake), flow control (sliding window), and error recovery.
5. Session Layer (Layer 5): Establishes, manages, synchronizes, and terminates communication dialogues and sessions between cooperating applications. Inserts synchronization checkpoints.
6. Presentation Layer (Layer 6): Handles data syntax, representation, and semantics. Manages character encoding (ASCII, UTF-8), data compression, and cryptographic encryption/decryption (SSL/TLS).
7. Application Layer (Layer 7): Provides network services directly to end-user software applications. Protocols: HTTP, HTTPS, FTP, DNS, SMTP, SSH.

+-------------------------------------------------------------------------+

sem_data.memorize: 7 Layers in order from bottom to top: Physical, Data Link, Network, Transport, Session, Presentation, Application (Mnemonic: 'Please Do Not Throw Sausage Pizza Away'). PDUs: Bits -> Frames -> Packets -> Segments -> Data.
sem_data.understand: Data Encapsulation: As data descends from Layer 7 to Layer 1, each layer wraps the payload with its own protocol header. At the receiving host, decapsulation strips headers layer-by-layer.
sem_data.common_mistakes: 1. Inverting layer numbering (Physical is Layer 1; Application is Layer 7). 2. Calling Transport Layer PDU a 'packet' (Transport is Segment; Network is Packet; Data Link is Frame).
sem_data.pyq_question: Explain the 7 layers of the OSI reference model with their primary functions. Differentiate between OSI and TCP/IP models. (15 Marks)
sem_data.pyq_rubric: Layer diagram with PDUs (4 marks) + Functions of 7 layers (7 marks) + OSI vs TCP/IP comparison table (4 marks) = 15 Marks.
model_answer_paragraphs: The Open Systems Interconnection (OSI) reference model, published by ISO in 1984, provides a standardized abstract framework enabling disparate computing systems to communicate. It decomposes the immense complexity of network protocols into seven modular layers, enforcing clean boundaries where each layer relies exclusively on services provided by lower layers.

• Layer 1 — Physical: Transmits raw bits over physical media (copper twisted pair, coaxial cable, optical fiber, radio frequencies). Defines pin layouts, voltage levels, signaling rates, and physical topology.
• Layer 2 — Data Link: Ensures hop-by-hop transmission between directly adjacent network nodes. Packages raw bits into Frames, arbitrates media access (MAC layer), detects transmission errors via Cyclic Redundancy Checks (CRC), and enforces frame-level flow control.
• Layer 3 — Network: Handles end-to-end routing of Packets across multiple intermediate network hops. Assigns logical addresses (IPv4/IPv6), calculates optimal paths via routing algorithms (Dijkstra, Bellman-Ford), and manages packet fragmentation.
• Layer 4 — Transport: Provides reliable or best-effort process-to-process communication. Manages port numbers (0-65535), segments byte streams, performs error recovery via sequence/acknowledgment numbers (TCP), and regulates transmission speed via sliding window flow control.
• Layer 5 — Session: Manages application dialogue sessions, providing simplex, half-duplex, or full-duplex communication and embedding synchronization checkpoints to prevent re-transmitting entire files upon connection loss.
• Layer 6 — Presentation: Translates network data formats. Performs character encoding (ASCII to UTF-8), cryptographic encryption/decryption (TLS/SSL), and compression/decompression algorithms.
• Layer 7 — Application: The user interface layer providing network services to end-user applications. Implements protocols like HTTP/HTTPS (web), DNS (name resolution), SMTP (mail), and SSH (secure shell).

At the sender, data travels downwards from Application to Physical. Each layer attaches its specific protocol header (and trailer at Data Link), transforming the PDU: Application Data --> Segments (Transport) --> Packets (Network) --> Frames (Data Link) --> Bits (Physical). At the receiver, decapsulation peels off headers in reverse.
4. Comparison: OSI Reference Model vs TCP/IP Protocol Suite:

While OSI is a conceptual model with 7 strict layers, TCP/IP is a practical 4-layer architecture that powers the global Internet. TCP/IP collapses Session, Presentation, and Application into a single Application layer, and merges Physical and Data Link into a Network Access layer. TCP/IP protocols were built first and standardized, whereas OSI standardized the model before creating commercial protocols.

apt_data.topic: Profit & Loss — Marked Price, Trade Discount, Cash Discount & Markup Formulas
tutorial: Marked Price (MP) or List Price: The price printed on the label or catalog of an article.

Discount is ALWAYS calculated on the Marked Price (MP), never on Cost Price:
• Discount = MP - SP    ==> Discount % = (Discount / MP) * 100
• Selling Price SP = MP * [1 - (Discount% / 100)]

Markup %: The percentage by which the retailer increases the Cost Price to arrive at the Marked Price:
• Markup = MP - CP      ==> Markup % = (Markup / CP) * 100
• MP = CP * [1 + (Markup% / 100)]

The Master Golden Equation connecting CP, MP, Profit% and Discount%:
SP = CP * [(100 + Profit%) / 100] = MP * [(100 - Discount%) / 100]
==> CP / MP = (100 - Discount%) / (100 + Profit%)
apt_data.formulas:
1. CP / MP = (100 - D%) / (100 + P%)
2. MP = CP * [(100 + Profit%) / (100 - Discount%)]
3. Single Equivalent Discount of d1% and d2%: D_net = [d1 + d2 - (d1 * d2) / 100]%
apt_data.shortcut:
The CP-MP Ratio Bridge (Instant Placement Solver):
If Discount = 10% and Profit = 20%, then:
CP / MP = (100 - 10) / (100 + 20) = 90 / 120 = 3 / 4.
If CP is Rs. 300, MP is instantly Rs. 400 without setting up multi-step equations!
apt_data.recognition: Look for 'after allowing a discount of x%, the trader makes a profit of y%', 'by how much percent should he mark his goods above CP to gain z% after giving a discount'.
apt_data.p1_q: [Foundation] A shopkeeper marks an article at Rs. 800 and offers a discount of 15%. What is the selling price of the article?
apt_data.p1_s:
Step 1: MP = Rs. 800, Discount = 15%.
Step 2: SP = MP * (1 - 0.15) = 800 * 0.85.
Step 3: Fast mental calculation: 800 * 0.85 = 8 * 85 = 8 * (80 + 5) = 640 + 40 = Rs. 680.
Answer: Selling Price is Rs. 680.
apt_data.p2_q: [Standard Placement] A trader marks his goods at such a price that after allowing a discount of 12.5% on the marked price, he still makes a profit of 20%. If the cost price of the article is Rs. 1,400, find its marked price.
apt_data.p3_source: [VERIFIED PUBLIC COMPANY QUESTION — TCS NQT 2024 Quantitative Section]
apt_data.p3_q: A merchant marks his goods 40% above the cost price. He sells half the stock at the marked price, one-quarter at a discount of 15% on the marked price, and the rest at a discount of 30% on the marked price. Find his overall gain percentage.
apt_data.p3_s:
Step 1: Choose convenient numbers:
Let total stock = 4 units, Cost Price of each unit = Rs. 100.
Total Cost Price (CP) = 4 * 100 = Rs. 400.
Marked Price (MP) per unit = 100 + 40% = Rs. 140.
Step 2: Calculate Selling Price for each portion:
- Half the stock (2 units) sold at MP = 2 * 140 = Rs. 280.
- One-quarter (1 unit) sold at 15% discount = 140 * (1 - 0.15) = 140 * 0.85 = Rs. 119.
- Rest of stock (4 - 2 - 1 = 1 unit) sold at 30% discount = 140 * (1 - 0.30) = 140 * 0.70 = Rs. 98.
Step 3: Total Selling Price (SP) = 280 + 119 + 98 = Rs. 497.
Step 4: Overall Profit = Total SP - Total CP = 497 - 400 = Rs. 97.
Overall Profit % = (97 / 400) * 100 = 97 / 4 = 24.25%.
Answer: Overall gain of 24.25%.
apt_data.p4_q: [Hard / Time-Pressure] A shopkeeper offers 'Buy 3 Get 1 Free' on branded t-shirts. In addition to this, he allows a further cash discount of 10% to customers paying in cash. What is the effective net percentage discount received by a cash-paying customer?
apt_data.p4_s:
Step 1: Analyze the 'Buy 3 Get 1 Free' offer:
Total articles received = 3 + 1 = 4 articles.
Free articles received = 1 article.
Initial Discount % from offer = [Free / Total Received] * 100 = (1 / 4) * 100 = 25% discount.
Step 2: Apply the additional 10% cash discount successively:
Net Discount % = [d1 + d2 - (d1 * d2) / 100]%
= [25 + 10 - (25 * 10) / 100]% = [35 - 250 / 100]% = 35 - 2.5 = 32.5%.
Alternative Value Method: Let MP of each t-shirt = Rs. 100. For 4 t-shirts, total MP = Rs. 400.
Customer pays for 3 t-shirts = Rs. 300.
10% cash discount on Rs. 300 = Rs. 30 discount ==> Customer pays 300 - 30 = Rs. 270.
Total Discount = 400 - 270 = Rs. 130 on Rs. 400.
Discount % = (130 / 400) * 100 = 32.5%.
Answer: Effective net discount is 32.5%.

apt_data.trap: In 'Buy X Get Y Free' schemes, NEVER calculate discount as (Y / X) * 100! The customer takes home (X + Y) items, so the true discount is always [Y / (X + Y)] * 100.
